prompt_payload.task: Design a diverse library of executable semantic optimization skills for finite-pool scientific search. Each skill defines interpretable rule features plus a conservative Bayesian linear surrogate blended with strong target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI anchors.

target.title: ChemLex acid-amine wetlab conversion replay
target.boundary: Field values and counts are public; target outcomes are not included.

source_transfer_evidence.boundary: No source identity, source schema, source outcomes, source effects, or source value priors are provided. The LLM must use the public target schema and its pretrained domain knowledge only.

executor.semantic_model: Rules become binary features. Revealed target outcomes fit a ridge Bayesian linear surrogate whose coefficient prior follows rule weights.
executor.anchor: A rank blend of target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI.
executor.fusion: semantic_mass_start/end controls the rank mass assigned to the semantic surrogate; the remaining mass stays on the target-only anchor.
executor.selection: Independent calibration seeds select one frozen skill. Independent held-out seeds are evaluated only after selection.

design_requirements: Use only exact field/value pairs in public_semantic_fields.

Each conditions object must map a real catalog field name directly to one exact catalog value, for example {"dominant_family": "oxide"}. Never use literal placeholder keys such as exact_field, field_name, field, or value.
Give every skill a distinct, descriptive scientific skill_id. Never copy schema placeholders such as short_unique_name or add numeric suffixes to a placeholder.
Give every skill 3-10 rules; use two-condition interactions only when scientifically meaningful.
Include at least one conservative low-semantic-mass skill.
Use only target-schema-compatible domain knowledge; do not imply that a source task or source outcomes were observed.
Include at least one domain-knowledge skill.
Include a counter-hypothesis skill that reverses or downweights an uncertain source relation.
Prefer mechanistic, chemically or physically interpretable rules over arbitrary coverage rules.
Use positive weights for conditions expected to improve the target objective and negative weights for risks.
Do not claim access to target outcomes and do not output candidate identifiers.
For ChemLex, prioritize reagent_coupling_family and acid/amine motif fields over coarse length bins.
For ChemLex, include chemically plausible two-condition acid/amine or substrate/reagent interactions.

rules.rationale: short scientific rationale

skills.hypothesis: what this skill transfers and when it may fail

cards.title: Gate-rejected transfer: real_suzuki_miyaura to real_buchwald_hartwig
cards.summary: All evidence modes failed calibration and fell back to the target acquisition portfolio.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.title: Layered transferable skill artifact
cards.summary: CARE 2.0 skill transfer should not be limited to acquisition-level score adjustment; a reusable skill should specify representation mapping, mechanism hypothesis, model binding, acquisition binding, gate/risk checks, and workflow boundaries.
cards.content: A layered transferable skill artifact records six linked layers. Representation layer: what source fields or descriptors can be mapped to the target task. Mechanism layer: what scientific hypothesis is being reused, such as role importance, descriptor relevance, solvation, sterics, electronics, or stability. Model layer: how the skill changes a surrogate model, embedding, kernel, feature transform, or uncertainty prior. Acquisition layer: how it changes candidate ranking, UCB/EI, exploration strength, or candidate filtering. Gate/risk layer: when the transfer is allowed, when it should be rejected, and what negative-transfer failure modes are known. Workflow layer: experiment constraints, budget, batch design, data reveal protocol, and audit outputs. This card is the intended CARE 2.0 abstraction behind the current transfer-weighted kernel experiments.

cards.title: Reusable semantic feature pattern: high_aromatic_content
cards.summary: For real_moleculenet_lipophilicity, use the LLM to define the high_aromatic_content feature partition, then fit its direction and magnitude from revealed target observations.
cards.content: Evidence mode: target_only. Rule prior: disabled. Reusable lesson: preserve the LLM-proposed feature partition, but calibrate or remove unsupported coefficient signs before held-out evaluation.

cards.title: Reusable semantic feature pattern: high_element_count
cards.summary: For real_matbench_expt_gap, use the LLM to define the high_element_count feature partition, then fit its direction and magnitude from revealed target observations.
cards.content: Evidence mode: target_only. Rule prior: disabled. Reusable lesson: preserve the LLM-proposed feature partition, but calibrate or remove unsupported coefficient signs before held-out evaluation.

cards.title: Reusable semantic feature pattern: branching_effect
cards.summary: For real_moleculenet_freesolv, use the LLM to define the branching_effect feature partition, then fit its direction and magnitude from revealed target observations.
cards.content: Evidence mode: source_schema_only. Rule prior: enabled. Reusable lesson: preserve the LLM-proposed feature partition, but calibrate or remove unsupported coefficient signs before held-out evaluation.

cards.title: BH-to-Suzuki confidence-discount transfer
cards.summary: Near-domain transfer plan from Buchwald-Hartwig factor evidence to Suzuki-Miyaura replay.
cards.content: Proposed transfer path: learn public factor evidence from Buchwald-Hartwig, abstract it into a support/confidence card, discount by reaction-domain distance, apply only bounded adjustments in Suzuki, and let the evidence gate authorize or reject each challenger. Compare no-transfer baseline versus transferred-skill-plus-gate on matched seeds.

care_knowledge_context.instruction: Use these public, previously archived cards only as reusable design lessons. Do not copy reported target values into a rule and do not imply that the current target outcomes were observed. Prefer lessons that survived held-out calibration.

rules.rationale: Aromatic amines participate in π-stacking and resonance stabilization of the transition state during nucleophilic acyl substitution.
Acids with a single carbonyl group offer optimal electrophilicity without steric hindrance.
Neutral amines are more nucleophilic and less prone to side reactions.

skills.hypothesis: This skill improves conversion by leveraging aromatic stabilization and neutral nucleophile reactivity; may fail with highly sterically hindered substrates.

rules.rationale: High nitrogen content in acids can lead to unwanted nucleophilic attack or formation of byproducts.
Acids with amide groups are prone to hydrolysis under reaction conditions.

skills.hypothesis: This skill reduces side reactions by minimizing nitrogen-rich functional groups; may underperform in systems requiring nitrogen-based catalysis.

rules.rationale: Aromatic reagents provide planar geometry that aligns with the acid's reaction site.
Highly branched reagents cause steric hindrance and reduce reaction efficiency.

skills.hypothesis: This skill promotes efficient coupling through steric compatibility; may fail in highly polar or non-planar systems.

rules.rationale: Acyclic acids are more soluble in aqueous media, improving reaction homogeneity.
Fewer hydrogen bond donors reduce aggregation and improve mass transfer.

skills.hypothesis: This skill enhances solubility and reaction homogeneity; may not perform well in systems requiring strong intermolecular interactions.

rules.rationale: High fraction of sp³-hybridized carbons leads to conformational stability and reduced reactivity with side chains.

skills.hypothesis: This skill promotes stable conformations that resist decomposition; may reduce reactivity in highly reactive systems.

rules.rationale: High sp³ content reduces polarity and minimizes unwanted interactions.
Aromatic heteroatoms can stabilize transition states in unintended ways.

skills.hypothesis: This skill reduces unwanted stabilization; may underperform in systems requiring aromatic stabilization.

rules.rationale: Phosphorus-containing reagents may undergo hydrolysis or form phosphine byproducts.

skills.hypothesis: This skill avoids phosphorus-based reagents to prevent side reactions; may limit access to certain coupling chemistries.

rules.rationale: Low logP values correlate with better aqueous solubility and mass transfer.

skills.hypothesis: This skill improves solubility and mass transfer; may not be effective in highly hydrophobic systems.

rules.rationale: High aromatic content in acids can reduce nucleophilic attack by stabilizing the ground state.

skills.hypothesis: This skill challenges the assumption that aromatic acids are more reactive; may be useful in systems where nucleophilic attack is a major pathway.

rules.rationale: Fused heteroaromatic systems provide electronic stabilization of reaction intermediates.

skills.hypothesis: This skill enhances intermediate stability; may fail in systems requiring rapid reaction kinetics.
